**Bizum, Bancomat and EPI to build joint European payments network in Madrid**

*A shared interoperability network is planned to launch in Madrid by 2027, extending instant payments across at least 13 countries and covering over 70% of the EU population.*

Spain's Bizum, Italy's Bancomat, the European Payments Initiative (EPI) and Nordic mobile payments group Vipps have agreed to establish a shared network called EPN, headquartered in Madrid, with a target launch in 2027. The network is designed to connect domestic instant payment schemes across Europe, enabling cross-border person-to-person and eventually merchant payments without routing through Visa or Mastercard rails.

Fernando Rodriguez, Bizum's deputy general director of international expansion, described the initiative as an extension of Spain's instant payments model into a wider European setting. The network would initially cover at least 13 countries, reaching more than 70% of the EU population. For Bizum, which already processes high volumes domestically, the move marks a shift from national utility to pan-European infrastructure partner.

The initiative sits squarely within the broader European payment sovereignty agenda that has gained momentum since the Bank of Finland and French Banking Federation both framed domestic payment independence as a strategic priority. Where Wero is EPI's consumer-facing wallet brand, EPN would provide the underlying interoperability layer connecting disparate national schemes, a piece of plumbing that has been missing from Europe's fragmented instant payments landscape.

*Sources: [Madrid will host the European hub for instant payments](https://www.democrata.es/en/economy/the-european-instant-payment-networks-choose-madrid-for-their-new-common-hub/) — Demócrata | [European payment groups to launch Madrid-based EPN network in 2027](https://www.telecompaper.com/news/european-payment-groups-to-launch-madrid-based-epn-network-in-2027--1584215) — Telecompaper | [European payments groups join forces to challenge US dominance](https://www.globalbankingandfinance.com/european-payments-groups-join-forces-lessen-us-reliance/) — Globalbankingandfinance | [Madrid to host new European network connecting Bizum with major payment systems](https://www.todoalicante.es/english/madrid-host-european-network-20260930020919-nt_amp.html) — Todoalicante*

**Citi goes live on Swift's instant payments scheme across multiple markets**

*The deployment gives corporate clients access to cross-border instant payments in several countries through a single account structure, building on Swift's push to make real-time settlement the default for correspondent banking.*

Citi has activated multiple markets on Swift's cross-border instant payments scheme, allowing bank clients to reach real-time payment networks in several jurisdictions through one account relationship. The move extends Citi's earlier commitment to expanding its instant payments network, which reached 300 partner banks in July.

Swift's scheme connects national instant payment systems, such as SEPA Instant in Europe and equivalents elsewhere, through the existing correspondent banking infrastructure rather than requiring new bilateral connections. Citi's multi-market go-live is among the more substantial deployments to date, given the bank's scale in corporate treasury and trade finance.

Cross-border instant payments are moving closer to a standard service offering for European corporate treasurers rather than a bespoke capability. The deployment also reinforces Swift's position as the connective layer between national real-time systems, at a time when alternative approaches from BIS projects to stablecoin networks are competing for the same corridor.

*Sources: [Citi launches multi-market instant payments on Swift scheme](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/48508/citi-launches-multi-market-instant-payments-on-swift-scheme?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed) — Finextra*

**Experian launches open banking cashflow product for SME lending decisions**

*The product delivers 500 bank transaction signals to commercial lenders, arriving weeks after the UK chancellor's open finance push prioritised SME credit access.*

Experian has launched Cashflow Attributes, a product that provides commercial lenders with 500 signals derived from business bank transaction data via open banking. The product is designed to give lenders a more granular picture of SME cash flow patterns than traditional credit bureau data alone, addressing a persistent gap in small business underwriting.

The launch follows UK chancellor Rachel Reeves's announcement on July 9 of an open finance push specifically focused on improving SME access to credit. Experian's product is one of the first major commercial deployments to act on that policy signal, translating open banking data access into a structured lending tool rather than a raw data feed.

The product reduces reliance on limited financial statement data that many small businesses struggle to provide. The 500-signal approach suggests Experian is positioning open banking data not as a supplement to existing credit scoring but as a primary input for commercial lending decisions, a shift that reshapes how SME creditworthiness is assessed across the UK market.

*Sources: [Experian Gives Business Lenders 500 Bank Transaction Signals to Fill SME Credit Gap](https://www.techtimes.com/articles/328343/20260930/experian-gives-business-lenders-500-bank-transaction-signals-fill-sme-credit-gap.htm) — Techtimes | [Experian launches cashflow attributes for commercial lenders](https://www.openbankingexpo.com/news/experian-launches-cashflow-attributes-for-commercial-lenders/) — Open Banking Expo*

**Nubank rules out Monzo acquisition in securities filing**

*A formal SEC denial ends days of speculation over what would have been the largest acquisition of a UK digital bank, leaving Monzo to choose between a fresh funding round and a potential IPO.*

Nu Holdings, Nubank's parent company, said on September 30 that it is not pursuing a transaction with Monzo. The statement, made in a securities filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission, was unusually direct for a company that normally declines to comment on deal speculation. "While we have a great deal of respect for Monzo, the company is not pursuing a transaction with Monzo," Nu said, adding that its capital allocation framework is unchanged and its focus remains on Brazil, Mexico, Colombia and its US expansion through Nu Global.

The denial follows reports on September 26 that the two digital banks had held early-stage talks over a deal valuing Monzo at between £8 billion and £10 billion. Monzo had engaged Morgan Stanley and Slaughter & May to advise on its options. Nu Holdings shares had fallen roughly 10% on Monday as investors priced in the risk of a large overseas acquisition; the stock recovered nearly 7% after the filing.

For Monzo, the question now is which of its remaining options to pursue. The bank reported £1.7 billion of revenue and £25.7 billion of deposits in its most recent fiscal year, and has 16 million accounts. A sale to Nu was one of two paths its board had been weighing alongside an equity fundraising at a valuation above £8 billion to fund expansion into mainland Europe. A London IPO had been under discussion but remains unconfirmed, with a US listing also being considered given Monzo's shareholder base.

*Sources: [Brazil's Nubank says it is not pursuing deal with Monzo](https://www.sharecast.com/news/news-and-announcements/nubank-rules-out-multi-billion-pound-tie-up-with-monzo--23726066.html) — Sharecast*
